sections.body: This field covers the practical work of turning AI research into funded projects. Artificial intelligence is now used in drafting proposals by pulling text from past papers, checking funder rules, estimating budgets, matching collaborators, and scoring likely success. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10767 extracted claims provides source material for these tasks. Tools in this section help a researcher reuse prior work without starting from a blank page. They also handle the tedious parts of compliance and budget formatting. The focus is on the administrative and strategic side of research, not on the science itself.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work here is uneven. Drafting from past work is fairly reliable when the source papers are clean and well structured, but it still needs a human to check accuracy and tone. Funder formatting and compliance tools can catch missing sections or wrong page limits, yet they often miss agency specific rules that change without notice. Budget tools can add up allowable costs, but they cannot know an institution's negotiated rates or a funder's hidden preferences. Finding collaborators works best when there is a large, current database of researchers, which this site does not fully have. Predicting proposal success remains the weakest area, because past funding decisions are rarely public and many factors are outside any model's view.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Drafting Proposals from Past Work to turn existing papers into a first draft, then move to Funder Formatting and Compliance to make that draft fit a specific call. Budgets and Allowable Costs handles the financial tables and cost categories after the narrative is set. Finding Collaborators helps fill gaps in expertise or geography once the scope is clear. Predicting Proposal Success is best used last, as a rough check on whether to invest more time, not as a final gate. Together these pages follow the order of writing a proposal, from raw material to final review.
